4:1.sourceText: Οὕτως ἡμᾶς λογιζέσθω ἄνθρωπος ὡς ὑπηρέτας Χριστοῦ καὶ οἰκονόμους μυστηρίων Θεοῦ.
4:1.targetText: Let a man so reckon us as officers of Christ, and stewards of the secrets of God,

4:2.sourceText: ὧδε λοιπὸν ζητεῖται ἐν τοῖς οἰκονόμοις ἵνα πιστός τις εὑρεθῇ.
4:2.targetText: and as to the rest, it is required in the stewards that one may be found faithful,

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ὧδε is the here/in-this-situation adverb. The pinned TR instead has the ὃ δέ wording reflected in LSV’s connective opening; this actual here adverb is not assigned to an English and conjunction.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV opens with and, corresponding to the TR δέ connective. Pinned N1904 instead prints the actual ὧδε here adverb without an independent δέ at this position.

4:3.sourceText: ἐμοὶ δὲ εἰς ἐλάχιστόν ἐστιν ἵνα ὑφ’ ὑμῶν ἀνακριθῶ ἢ ὑπὸ ἀνθρωπίνης ἡμέρας· ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἀνακρίνω·
4:3.targetText: and to me it is for a very little thing that by you I may be judged, or by man’s Day, but I do not even judge myself,

groups.note: Actual ἐλάχιστον is the substantive superlative least/very-little adjective, rendered a very little thing; no separate Greek thing noun is printed.
Actual ἀνθρωπίνης is the human adjective modifying day. English man’s expresses that human qualifier possessively; no separately printed Greek genitive man noun is claimed.

4:4.sourceText: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐμαυτῷ σύνοιδα, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐν τούτῳ δεδικαίωμαι· ὁ δὲ ἀνακρίνων με Κύριός ἐστιν.
4:4.targetText: for I have been conscious of nothing for myself, but I have not been declared right in this—and He who is discerning me is the LORD:

4:5.sourceText: ὥστε μὴ πρὸ καιροῦ τι κρίνετε, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ Κύριος, ὃς καὶ φωτίσει τὰ κρυπτὰ τοῦ σκότους καὶ φανερώσει τὰς βουλὰς τῶν καρδιῶν· καὶ τότε ὁ ἔπαινος γενήσεται ἑκάστῳ ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ.
4:5.targetText: so, then, judge nothing before the time, until the LORD may come, who will both bring to light the hidden things of the darkness, and will reveal the counsels of the hearts, and then the praise will come to each from God.

groups.note: Actual γενήσεται is the future become/be predicate, rendered will come with praise. The source remains γίνομαι rather than an invented ἔρχομαι coming verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with God.

4:6.sourceText: Ταῦτα δέ, ἀδελφοί, μετεσχημάτισα εἰς ἐμαυτὸν καὶ Ἀπολλῶν δι’ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἐν ἡμῖν μάθητε τό Μὴ ὑπὲρ ἃ γέγραπται, ἵνα μὴ εἷς ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἑνὸς φυσιοῦσθε κατὰ τοῦ ἑτέρου.
4:6.targetText: And these things, brothers, I transferred to myself and to Apollos because of you, that in us you may learn not to think above that which has been written, that you may not be puffed up one for one against the other,

groups.note: The one actual εἰς before myself governs the coordinated myself and Apollos recipients. English repeats to with Apollos; both directed relations retain that one printed Greek preposition identity.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article τὸ introduces the quoted not-beyond-what-is-written maxim after learn. English does not separately render an article or nominal quotation label here.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes the think infinitive corroborated by the longer TR φρονεῖν reading. Pinned N1904 has the quoted not-beyond-what-is-written words without an independently written thinking verb.

4:7.sourceText: τίς γάρ σε διακρίνει; τί δὲ ἔχεις ὃ οὐκ ἔλαβες; εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔλαβες, τί καυχᾶσαι ὡς μὴ λαβών;
4:7.targetText: for who makes you to differ? And what do you have, that you did not receive? And if you also received, why do you glory as not having received?

4:8.sourceText: ἤδη κεκορεσμένοι ἐστέ· ἤδη ἐπλουτήσατε· χωρὶς ἡμῶν ἐβασιλεύσατε· καὶ ὄφελόν γε ἐβασιλεύσατε, ἵνα καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμῖν συνβασιλεύσωμεν.
4:8.targetText: Already you are having been filled, already you were rich, apart from us you reigned, and I also wish you reigned, that we also may reign together with you,

groups.note: Actual ὄφελον is the fixed wish expression and γε its emphatic particle; together LSV renders I also wish. This is not a separately printed θέλω wish verb or independent first-person pronoun. Primary lexical entry:https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/ophelon .
Actual dative ὑμῖν expresses the people joined in the reign-together compound predicate. English with you realizes that relation without an independently printed Greek with preposition.

4:9.sourceText: δοκῶ γάρ, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ἐσχάτους ἀπέδειξεν ὡς ἐπιθανατίους, ὅτι θέατρον ἐγενήθημεν τῷ κόσμῳ καὶ ἀγγέλοις καὶ ἀνθρώποις.
4:9.targetText: for I think that God set forth us the apostles last—as appointed to death, because we became a spectacle to the world, and messengers, and men;

groups.note: Actual ἐπιθανατίους is the death-doomed/condemned-to-death adjective, rendered appointed to death; no separate Greek appointment verb is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with God.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the God-set-forth content clause after think with that. Pinned N1904 proceeds directly from I-think to the God clause without a separate content conjunction.

4:10.sourceText: ἡμεῖς μωροὶ διὰ Χριστόν, ὑμεῖς δὲ φρόνιμοι ἐν Χριστῷ· ἡμεῖς ἀσθενεῖς, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰσχυροί· ὑμεῖς ἔνδοξοι, ἡμεῖς δὲ ἄτιμοι.
4:10.targetText: we [are] fools because of Christ, and you wise in Christ; we [are] ailing, and you strong; you glorious, and we dishonored;

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the first copula in the parallel adjective descriptions; no Greek be verb is independently printed here.
English supplies the second bracketed copula with the ailing adjective; no Greek be verb is independently printed in this parallel clause.

4:11.sourceText: ἄχρι τῆς ἄρτι ὥρας καὶ πεινῶμεν καὶ διψῶμεν καὶ γυμνιτεύομεν καὶ κολαφιζόμεθα καὶ ἀστατοῦμεν
4:11.targetText: to the present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are battered, and wander,

4:12.sourceText: καὶ κοπιῶμεν ἐργαζόμενοι ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσίν· λοιδορούμενοι εὐλογοῦμεν, διωκόμενοι ἀνεχόμεθα,
4:12.targetText: and labor, working with [our] own hands; being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we endure;

groups.note: Actual ἰδίαις is the own adjective for the hands belonging to the first-person workers. English [our] own realizes that same subject-owned relation; no separate Greek ἡμῶν personal possessive is printed.

4:13.sourceText: δυσφημούμενοι παρακαλοῦμεν· ὡς περικαθάρματα τοῦ κόσμου ἐγενήθημεν, πάντων περίψημα ἕως ἄρτι.
4:13.targetText: being spoken evil of, we plead; we became as filth of the world—of all things an outcast—until now.

groups.note: Actual περίψημα is the wiped-off/refuse noun, rendered an outcast for discarded/rejected material or status. Its source remains that refuse head, not a Greek exile or banishment verb. Primary lexical entry:https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/peripsema .

4:14.sourceText: Οὐκ ἐντρέπων ὑμᾶς γράφω ταῦτα, ἀλλ’ ὡς τέκνα μου ἀγαπητὰ νουθετῶν.
4:14.targetText: Not [as] putting you to shame do I write these things, but I admonish as my beloved children,

groups.note: The actual shaming participle modifies the writing predicate. English [as] putting ... to shame makes that same manner relation explicit without a separately printed initial Greek as word.

Actual νουθετῶν is a present admonishing participle under the first-person writer’s predicate. LSV expresses it as finite I admonish; no additional independently written personal I pronoun or finite admonishing form is claimed.

4:15.sourceText: ἐὰν γὰρ μυρίους παιδαγωγοὺς ἔχητε ἐν Χριστῷ, ἀλλ’ οὐ πολλοὺς πατέρας· ἐν γὰρ Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ διὰ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἐγὼ ὑμᾶς ἐγέννησα.
4:15.targetText: for if a myriad of child-conductors you may have in Christ, yet not many fathers; for in Christ Jesus, through the good news, I begot you;

4:16.sourceText: παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς, μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε.
4:16.targetText: I call on you, therefore, become followers of me;

4:17.sourceText: Διὰ τοῦτο αὐτὸ ἔπεμψα ὑμῖν Τιμόθεον, ὅς ἐστίν μου τέκνον ἀγαπητὸν καὶ πιστὸν ἐν Κυρίῳ, ὃς ὑμᾶς ἀναμνήσει τὰς ὁδούς μου τὰς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, καθὼς πανταχοῦ ἐν πάσῃ ἐκκλησίᾳ διδάσκω.
4:17.targetText: because of this I sent to you Timotheus, who is my child, beloved and faithful in the LORD, who will remind you of my ways in Christ, according as everywhere in every assembly I teach.

groups.note: The actual accusative article/ways phrase is the content object of reminding. English realizes that content as of my ways; no independent Greek of preposition or genitive noun case is printed here.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual αὐτό intensifies this cause as this very/same cause. English because of this does not separately express that emphatic word; it is not a second independent personal object pronoun here.
The repeated Greek article introduces the in-Christ qualifier of ways; English does not separately render this attributive article.
Pinned N1904 writes Christ Jesus here. LSV names Christ without separately rendering the Jesus name, corroborated by the shorter TR Christ reading.

4:18.sourceText: ὡς μὴ ἐρχομένου δέ μου πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐφυσιώθησάν τινες·
4:18.targetText: And some were puffed up as if I were not coming to you;

groups.note: Actual coming participle with genitive μου forms the as-if-I-not-coming construction. English were coming makes that same verbal circumstance finite without changing the original participial form.
Actual μου is the genitive first-person subject of the genitive-absolute coming phrase, rendered nominative I in English. No nominative Greek ἐγώ token is substituted.

4:19.sourceText: ἐλεύσομαι δὲ ταχέως πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐὰν ὁ Κύριος θελήσῃ, καὶ γνώσομαι οὐ τὸν λόγον τῶν πεφυσιωμένων ἀλλὰ τὴν δύναμιν·
4:19.targetText: but I will come quickly to you, if the LORD may will, and I will not know the word of those puffed up, but the power;

4:20.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ ἐν λόγῳ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἀλλ’ ἐν δυνάμει.
4:20.targetText: for not in word is the Kingdom of God, but in power.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula for the Kingdom description; pinned N1904 has the noun subject and manner phrases without an independently written be verb.

4:21.sourceText: τί θέλετε; ἐν ῥάβδῳ ἔλθω πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἢ ἐν ἀγάπῃ πνεύματί τε πραΰτητος;
4:21.targetText: What do you wish? Will I come to you with a rod, or in love, also with a spirit of meekness?

groups.note: Actual ἔλθω is the first-person aorist subjunctive in a deliberative question, rendered Will I come. Its source is not relabeled as a Greek future indicative.
